pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis (secondary to an Ovarian Teratoma) THE SMOKING GUN: The presence of a complex pelvic mass (ovarian teratoma) combined with orofacial dyskinesias, severe autonomic instability, and the pathognomonic 'extreme delta brush' pattern on EEG. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: The patient's ovarian teratoma contained ectopic neural tissue expressing NMDA (N-methyl-D-aspartate) receptors. This triggered a systemic autoantibody response against the GluN1 subunit of the NMDA receptor. These autoantibodies crossed the blood-brain barrier, causing cross-linking and selective internalization of post-synaptic NMDA receptors in the central nervous system. The loss of NMDA receptor function disrupts frontostriatal and limbic networks, driving the classic clinical progression: early psychiatric symptoms, followed by movement disorders, dysautonomia, and hypoventilation. Surgical excision of the teratoma combined with early immunotherapy (plasma exchange, IVIG, and high-dose corticosteroids) is crucial for clinical recovery.
